title: Microsoft Agent 365: registry sync from external AI platforms
summary: The briefing's licensing, controls, opt-in behaviour and roadmap dates are supported by Microsoft's documentation. The remaining corrections are minor: complete the abbreviated checklist navigation and remove synchronization instructions that have no corresponding control row.

claims.claim: Connecting an external platform discovers supported agents and adds them to the Microsoft 365 agent registry.
claims.quote: After you create a connection, Agent 365 can discover supported agents and add them to the Microsoft 365 agent registry.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes discovering external agents and automatically syncing them for visibility and governance.
claims.quote: Connect to external AI platforms to discover agents created outside Microsoft and automatically sync them into the Agent 365 registry for more complete agent visibility and governance.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn calls the feature Connected platforms in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Create and manage external platform connections from the Connected platforms page in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: The supported-platform table lists seven platforms with agent synchronization.
claims.quote: Amazon Bedrock; Google Vertex AI; Salesforce Agentforce; Databricks Genie; Anthropic Claude; Oracle Generative AI Agents; Snowflake Cortex

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; controls[0].note; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Agent 365 AI administrator creates and manages connections in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: The Agent 365 AI administrator creates and manages the connection in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; controls[0].note; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: The platform administrator owns the source account and prepares credentials and permissions.
claims.quote: The platform administrator controls the source account and its credentials; the Agent 365 administrator manages the connection and reviews the resulting inventory.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: Synchronization is manual, started by an administrator using Sync agents, subject to the stated Databricks first-run exception.
claims.quote: After you save the connection, select Sync agents to start synchronization. You need to manually synchronize the agents.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Open questions
claims.claim: Synchronization does not currently run on a schedule.
claims.quote: Manual synchronization only. Agent 365 doesn't currently sync on a schedule, and Microsoft doesn't prescribe a fixed synchronization interval.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Open questions
claims.claim: Deleting an agent from its source platform is not guaranteed to remove its registry entry.
claims.quote: Synchronization doesn't currently guarantee that an agent removed from the source platform is automatically removed from the Microsoft 365 agent registry.

claims.claim: The general connection guide instructs administrators to select Sync agents after saving.
claims.quote: After you save the connection, select Sync agents to start synchronization.

claims.claim: Saving a Databricks Genie connection starts its first synchronization automatically.
claims.quote: When you save the connection, the details pane opens and starts the first synchronization.

claims.claim: Later Databricks synchronization runs use Sync agents.
claims.quote: To synchronize after you create or share more Genie agents, open the connection and select Sync agents.

claims.claim: Registry sync gives visibility and governance for externally built and hosted agents.
claims.quote: Registry sync (the connected platforms feature described in this article) gives you visibility and governance for agents that you don't build or host yourself.

claims.claim: Registry sync does not add code-level capabilities.
claims.quote: Registry sync doesn't add code-level capabilities.

claims.where: front matter: status; What's changing; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.where: front matter: previewDate; What's changing; Scope

claims.quote: "previewDate": "May CY2026"

claims.where: front matter: targetDate; What's changing; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap general availability target is July CY2026, not a commitment.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "July CY2026"

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant).
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.where: front matter: platforms; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap platform is Web.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.claim: The roadmap release phases are General Availability and Preview.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.claim: Learn documents an available connection experience despite the roadmap's In development status.
claims.quote: Use the Connected platforms page to connect supported third-party agent platforms to Microsoft Agent 365.

claims.claim: The integration-options page labels registry sync as preview.
claims.quote: | Registry sync (preview) | Connected agent platforms, such as Google Vertex AI and Amazon Bedrock. | Configured per platform. Imports agents for visibility and governance. | No |

claims.claim: Coverage depends on the source platform and does not guarantee inclusion of every source agent.
claims.quote: Coverage depends on the connected platform and the agents it exposes, so a registry entry represents the supported information available from that source - not a guarantee that every agent on the platform is included.

claims.claim: Supported external agents appear in the same inventory as Microsoft and in-house agents.
claims.quote: The agent registry in the Microsoft 365 admin center lists the agents in your organization. It includes agents from Microsoft, from partners, and from your own teams.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Registry sync is admin-opt-in: an administrator must create a connection before synchronization can occur.
claims.quote: After you create a connection, Agent 365 can discover supported agents and add them to the Microsoft 365 agent registry.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Connection credentials are stored as encrypted connection data within Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: Agent 365 stores the credentials that you enter for a connection as encrypted connection data within Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: Every currently supported platform needs a key-based credential such as an API key, secret or private key.
claims.quote: Every currently supported platform requires a key-based credential, such as an API key, secret, or private key.

claims.claim: Connected platforms does not currently support keyless authentication such as workload identity federation or role assumption.
claims.quote: Keyless authentication options, such as workload identity federation or role assumption, aren't currently supported for Connected platforms.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Collect agent observability data is enabled by default on new connections.
claims.quote: New connections have this setting enabled by default.

claims.claim: Observability collection retrieves source-platform agent activity telemetry using the stored credentials.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 retrieves agent activity telemetry—such as agent sessions, usage, and related operational signals—from the connected platform by using the connection's stored credentials.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Telemetry retrieval can query provider logging or data services, including Google BigQuery and Amazon S3.
claims.quote: Retrieving agent telemetry from the connected platform might query the provider's own logging or data services (for example, Google BigQuery or Amazon S3)

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Observability retrieval can incur provider-billed data-access or query charges.
claims.quote: can incur data access or query charges that the provider bills. Review your provider's pricing before you enable collection.

claims.claim: Connections are read-only by design and Agent 365 does not invoke, execute or interact with source agents.
claims.quote: Connected platform connections are read-only by design: Agent 365 never invokes, executes, or interacts with agents in the source platform.

claims.claim: Agent 365 does not write to the source platform except when an administrator explicitly removes a synchronized agent.
claims.quote: Agent 365 doesn't write to, modify, or delete resources in the source platform. The only exception is an explicit administrator action to remove a synchronized agent

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The general security model says source deletion requires a separate optional delete permission that can be withheld.
claims.quote: an explicit administrator action to remove a synchronized agent, which requires a separate, optional delete permission that you can choose not to grant.

claims.claim: The Google guide includes aiplatform.reasoningEngines.delete in the permissions to grant.
claims.quote: Grant the service account the Vertex AI permissions required for agent discovery and management: aiplatform.reasoningEngines.list aiplatform.reasoningEngines.get aiplatform.reasoningEngines.delete

claims.claim: Databricks Genie activity collection requires Can Manage permission.
claims.quote: Activity requires Can Manage. Databricks returns the conversations of all users of a Genie agent only to principals that have Can Manage permission.

claims.claim: Databricks Can Manage also permits moving the source agent to the trash when an administrator removes it in Agent 365.
claims.quote: when an administrator removes a synchronized agent in Agent 365 and the service principal has Can Manage permission on the Genie agent. In that case, Agent 365 moves the Genie agent to the trash in Databricks.

claims.claim: Agent 365 uses fixed outbound IP addresses that restricted source networks must allow.
claims.quote: Agent 365 calls source platform APIs from a fixed set of outbound IP addresses. If your organization restricts network access to a source platform, allow traffic from these addresses before you create the connection.

claims.claim: Source-network restrictions can produce an authentication error despite correct credentials.
claims.quote: When a network restriction blocks Agent 365, the connection can fail with the message Authentication failed. Please check your credentials and try again., even when the credentials are correct.

claims.claim: The synchronization documentation describes no autonomous agent behaviour.
claims.quote: Searched: Agent 365 registry sync automatic rollout default connection schedule; read Connected platforms, integration options and Databricks guides. Documented sync is administrator-triggered, including saving the first Databricks connection, and never invokes source agents.

claims.claim: The registry represents the last synchronization rather than continuously current source state.
claims.quote: Agent 365 doesn't currently sync on a schedule ... Re-run Sync agents after you add, update, or remove agents in the source platform, and before reviews that depend on current registry data.

claims.claim: Oracle Generative AI Agents observability is marked Coming soon.
claims.quote: | Oracle Generative AI Agents | Generative AI Agents | Yes | Coming soon |

claims.claim: Snowflake Cortex observability is marked Coming soon.
claims.quote: | Snowflake Cortex | Cortex Agents | Yes | Coming soon |

claims.claim: Databricks Genie observability is available through Frontier.
claims.quote: Databricks Genie observability is available through the Frontier program.

claims.claim: The observability collection control is Frontier preview subject to existing customer-agreement preview terms.
claims.quote: This feature is part of Frontier preview program ... Frontier previews are subject to the existing preview terms of your customer agreements.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The Agent 365 overview states that the product is licensed per user.
claims.quote: Microsoft Agent 365 is licensed on a per-user basis.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The overview requires at least one qualifying licensed user to enable Agent 365.
claims.quote: At least one user must be licensed with a qualifying Microsoft Agent 365 license to enable Agent 365.

claims.claim: The overview says Agent 365 works best with Microsoft E5 as a prerequisite.
claims.quote: Microsoft Agent 365 works best when using Microsoft E5 as a pre-requisite.

claims.claim: The overview directs readers to the product pricing page and service description for plan details.
claims.quote: For plans and pricing information, see Microsoft Agent 365: The Control Plane for Agents. For details on feature availability by plan, see the Microsoft Agent 365 service description.

claims.claim: The Connected platforms page itself names no separate registry-sync licence or price.
claims.quote: Searched: Agent 365 connected platforms registry synchronization pricing billing meter license; read the complete Connected platforms page, including its prerequisites, lifecycle and provider-charge note. It names no separate registry-sync licence or price.

claims.claim: The roadmap record names no licence or price.
claims.quote: "description": "Connect to external AI platforms to discover agents created outside Microsoft and automatically sync them into the Agent 365 registry for more complete agent visibility and governance."

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Registry sync is included as a core capability with a Microsoft cloud subscription in the service-description table.
claims.quote: Core capability included with Microsoft cloud subscription | Premium capability | GCC Availability; Synchronize 3P agents and agent metadata from external platforms not managed by Microsoft into the Agent 365 registry (Connected Platforms) | Microsoft 365 admin center | Yes | Yes | Yes

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The same table also marks Connected Platforms synchronization Yes under Premium capability.
claims.quote: | Synchronize 3P agents and agent metadata from external platforms not managed by Microsoft into the Agent 365 registry (Connected Platforms) | Microsoft 365 admin center | Yes | Yes | Yes |

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no Microsoft meter for registry sync.
claims.quote: Searched: Agent 365 connected platforms registry synchronization pricing billing meter license; read Connected platforms, overview, service description and microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365 pricing. Found subscription entitlements and provider charges, not a Microsoft registry-sync meter.

claims.claim: Feature rollout mechanics are not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: Agent 365 registry sync tenant disable switch automatic rollout default connection schedule; read roadmap, Connected platforms, overview and integration options. No feature rollout ring, deployment window or automatic tenant-enablement mechanics are given.

claims.claim: Registry sync does not require agent code changes.
claims.quote: Registry sync (the connected platforms feature described in this article) gives you visibility and governance for agents that you don't build or host yourself. It doesn't require code changes.

claims.claim: The creation route is Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All Agents > Connected platforms > Manage > + Connect a platform.
claims.quote: In the navigation pane, select Agents > All Agents. In the Connected platforms web part, select Manage. Select + Connect a platform.

claims.claim: No administrative API or command for creating, editing or deleting external-platform connections is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Agent 365 Connected platforms connection management Sync agents Microsoft Graph API PowerShell; "Connected platforms" "API" "connection" "Agent 365". Read Connected platforms, Graph guide and Package Management API overview; no connection-management operation found.

claims.claim: The observability route opens Connected platforms through Manage, selects a connection, edits it and changes Collect agent observability data.
claims.quote: Open the Connected platforms page in the Microsoft 365 admin center. Create a new connection, or select an existing connection and edit it. Select or clear Collect agent observability data.

claims.claim: No API or command to change a connection's observability collection setting is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Agent 365" "observability" "Collect" "Graph" "connection" API PowerShell; read Connected platforms, Graph guide and Package Management API overview. Found the connection-dialog checkbox, not a matching API property or command.

claims.claim: No tenant-wide registry-sync off switch is documented on either UI or automation surfaces.
claims.quote: Searched: Agent 365 registry sync tenant disable switch automatic rollout default connection schedule; read Connected platforms, Agent settings, Graph guide, Package Management API overview and Troubleshoot connected platforms. Found per-connection removal, not a tenant-wide sync switch.

claims.claim: Clearing Collect agent observability data stops new collection for that connection.
claims.quote: When you clear this setting, Microsoft 365 stops collecting new observability data for that connection's agents.

claims.claim: Earlier telemetry remains subject to the registry's existing retention and management behaviour.
claims.quote: The agent registry retains telemetry collected earlier according to its existing retention and management behavior.

claims.claim: Credential rotation, changing scope and revoking access follow the relevant platform guide.
claims.quote: When you need to rotate credentials, change the source scope, revoke access, or remove the connection, follow the relevant provider guide.

claims.claim: Agent settings lists management rules, agent and plugin access, security templates, sharing, user access, feedback sharing and tags.
claims.quote: Agent management rules; Agent and plugin access; Security templates; Sharing; User access; Agent feedback sharing; Tags

claims.claim: Microsoft does not specifically state whether agent and plugin access settings govern externally synced agents.
claims.quote: Searched: Agent 365 synced external connected platforms agents agent plugin access user access settings applicability; read Agent settings, Connected platforms and connect-existing-agents search passage. Catalog installation controls do not explicitly include externally hosted sync-only agents.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not specifically state whether user access settings govern externally synced agents.
claims.quote: Searched: Agent 365 synced external connected platforms agents agent plugin access user access settings applicability; read Agent settings and Connected platforms. User access addresses Copilot access and installation; source agents continue running externally and are not invoked by registry sync.

claims.claim: No administrative API or PowerShell route for running Sync agents is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Agent 365 Connected platforms connection management Sync agents Microsoft Graph API PowerShell; "Connected platforms" "API" "connection" "Agent 365". Read Connected platforms, Graph guide and Package Management API overview; found no synchronization operation.

claims.claim: The documented Graph registry APIs can list agents in the tenant inventory.
claims.quote: Get all agents in your inventory: Use the List packages API, to retrieve a complete list of agents in your tenant for compliance and reporting.

claims.claim: The Graph registry references do not document connection management or synchronization operations.
claims.quote: Searched: connection and synchron in fetched List packages reference; read Get Copilot package details and Package Management API overview API list. Operations concern packages, requests and policy templates, not external-platform connections or Sync agents.

claims.claim: Registry-sync documentation describes no change to the source agents' end-user experience.
claims.quote: Searched: Agent 365 registry sync automatic rollout default connection schedule; read Connected platforms and connected-platforms guidance. Agents continue running where built; registry sync never invokes or interacts with source agents. No end-user experience change is described.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout, Create the connection
claims.claim: The checklist locates connection creation under Agents > All Agents > Connected platforms.
claims.quote: In the navigation pane, select Agents > All Agents. In the Connected platforms web part, select Manage. Select + Connect a platform.
claims.fix: Expand the checklist route to 'Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All Agents > Connected platforms > Manage > + Connect a platform', as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/connected-platforms.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout and After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The checklist instructs administrators to start and re-run Sync agents, but the controls table has no synchronization row.
claims.quote: Start synchronisation ... Re-run Sync agents on a cadence you choose ... Controls: Creating, editing and deleting connections; Whether observability data is collected; Tenant-wide switch to turn registry sync off.
claims.fix: The 'Start synchronisation' and 'Re-run Sync agents' checklist steps have no corresponding control row. Remove these checklist instructions during correction; retain the already documented synchronization explanation in What's changing rather than adding an unchecked row.

Whether observability data is collected for a connection's agents
